name: Overnight French Toast Casserole with Raspberries & Maple Syrup

instructions.primary_message: Cut bread loaf into 1-inch cubes. Transfer to a large baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. Set out on the counter to dry out overnight. (Alternatively, if short on time, place baking sheet in a preheated 200°F oven for 30-35 minutes. Let cool completely before proceeding to the next step.)
When the bread is dried out, coat a 9 x 13-inch baking dish with butter. Transfer bread cubes to the baking dish, spread out in an even layer, and set aside.
Place additional butter in a small saucepan and melt over medium heat. Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place eggs, vanilla, and spices in a medium bowl; whisk to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp vanilla extract
½ tsp cinnamon, ground
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp nutmeg, ground

instructions.primary_message: Add melted butter, milk, and sugar to the bowl with the egg. Whisk once more to combine the custard.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 cup whole milk
½ cup granulated sugar

instructions.primary_message: Pour custard over the bread in the baking dish. Cover the dish with aluminum foil and place in the fridge for a minimum of 4 hours and up to 12 hours.

When you're ready to bake the casserole, discard foil from baking dish and place in a cold oven. Preheat oven to 350°F; once the oven comes to temperature, bake the casserole for 50-60 minutes until golden brown on top and the custard is set in the middle. Remove from oven and let cool slightly.
Right before serving, wash and dry raspberries.
To serve, cut casserole into portions and divide between plates; top with raspberries and maple syrup. Serve with butter and enjoy!
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup pure maple syrup
3 tbsp butter, unsalted
